name: Toyota 4Runner
drivetrain: RWD or part-time 4WD (full-time 4WD with a locking center diff on Limited); available KDSS and a locking rear diff on TRD trims
reliability: 9/10 — the fifth-gen 4Runner is old-school body-on-frame engineering, and that is exactly why people love it. The 4.0L 1GR-FE V6 and the 5-speed automatic are ancient by modern standards but genuinely bulletproof, with very few chronic failures and a huge base of 200k–300k-mile trucks. The trade-offs are all about the dated platform: it is thirsty, the interior and tech are behind the times, and the 5-speed is down two or three ratios versus rivals. If you want durability and real off-road ability, few things hold up like it.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate · Maintenance ~$500/yr · Fuel economy is its weak point (~18 mpg real-world) · Class-leading resale — clean 4Runners are notoriously hard to buy used because owners keep them
popular_mods: A dedicated set of all-terrain tires — the highest-impact upgrade for looks and capability
A mild lift (or just better shocks) to fit larger tires and improve travel
Skid plates, sliders, and a light bar for genuine off-road use
Roof rack, drawer/storage systems, and a fridge slide for overlanding
Honest take: the 4Runner is a durable off-roader, not a fast or efficient SUV — spend on tires, protection, and suspension, not power
oil_interval: Per the Maintenance Minder (~5,000–7,500 miles; many owners run 5,000)

generations.4th Gen N210 (2003–2009 US): The last 4Runner with an available V8 (4.7L) alongside the V6 — beloved and very durable, if getting old now.
generations.5th Gen N280 (2010–2024 US): One of the longest production runs in the segment — 4.0L V6, 5-speed automatic, real 4WD hardware, and a reputation for outlasting almost everything. Dated on-road, superb off-road and for resale.
generations.6th Gen (2025+ US): A ground-up redesign moving to a turbocharged four (including an i-FORCE MAX hybrid) and an 8-speed automatic — far more modern, but a clean fifth-gen is the proven used pick.

common_issues: Poor fuel economy and an aging 5-speed automatic — the price of the old-school platform, not a defect
Dated infotainment and interior versus newer rivals (improved slightly in the 2020 refresh)
A stiff, jittery unladen ride on some trims; the KDSS-equipped trucks ride and handle better
Body/frame surface rust in heavy road-salt regions — inspect the frame on Northern trucks
Some owners note the tailgate/rear-window mechanism and the small third-row option as quirks, not faults
maintenance_tips: Change the 0W-20 oil on time — the 1GR V6 is happiest on a shorter interval
Service the transfer case and differential fluids on schedule, especially if you actually go off-road or tow
Inspect and treat the frame for rust in salt-belt states — it is the main thing that ends these trucks
Keep the 5-speed automatic fluid fresh despite 'lifetime' claims
Confirm any open recalls by VIN, and check that off-road trucks have not been abused

engine.detail: Old-school 4.0L naturally-aspirated V6 (1GR-FE), 270 hp - no turbos, no direct injection, one of Toyota's most proven engines.
engine.watch: Genuinely bulletproof; higher-mile trucks may show minor water-pump or valve-cover gasket seepage. It's just thirsty (~18 mpg real-world), which is the platform, not a defect.

drivetrain.detail: 5-speed automatic (A750) driving RWD or real part-time 4WD; Limited runs full-time 4WD, and TRD trims add a locking rear diff and KDSS.
drivetrain.watch: The 5-speed and 4WD hardware are very durable - just down a couple of gears versus rivals. Service the transfer-case and diff fluids on schedule if you tow or go off-road.

suspension.detail: Body-on-frame with a coil-sprung rear; some trims offer KDSS, which stiffens the anti-roll bars only when needed for a better ride and off-road flex.
suspension.watch: No chronic faults; the ride is just firm and jittery unladen on some trims - KDSS-equipped trucks ride and handle noticeably better.

body.detail: Traditional body-on-frame SUV built for durability and off-road abuse rather than car-like refinement.
body.watch: Main long-term killer is frame and control-arm surface rust in road-salt states - inspect the frame closely on Northern trucks; Southern trucks rarely have issues.
